register: Estimate-class dollar attachment to the verified criterion flip census (order-free: published stars versus the stars under the stated minimum computed exactly on the full trimmed sample; runs/criterion_census.json, independently recounted in runs/criterion_recount_stored.json). The headline basis is the criterion census at the order-free exact optimum; the earlier basis, the 23 flips exact at the four-order collapse envelope, is kept as the prior-basis record. Everything dollar-denominated is an estimate, not exact: single-month enrollment snapshots joined by contract ID; $500/enrollee/yr midpoint with a $400-$600 band from public actuarial and policy commentary. Misallocation framing: gross, two-directional, payments to the wrong insurers; never a net-cost-to-taxpayer claim; net fields are record-side only and never print.

inputs.flip_set: runs/criterion_census.json flips_criterion (qbp_priceable rows), verified by the stored recount runs/criterion_recount_stored.json
inputs.prior_basis: runs/dollar_estimate_collapse23.json (the 23 flips exact at the collapse envelope; prior basis)

estimate_basis.what_it_represents: Approximate annual MA revenue difference per enrollee between QBP bonus status (>=4.0 stars: 5% benchmark bonus, 10% in double-bonus counties) and non-bonus status (<4.0), the boundary every contract in this set crosses.

public_reference_figures.source: KFF, 'Medicare Will Spend More Than $13 Billion on the Medicare Advantage Quality Bonus Program in 2026' (Biniek, Ochieng, Freed; July 1, 2026)
public_reference_figures.figures: QBP spending $13.4B in 2026 across ~24M bonus-plan enrollees (~$560/enrollee average); segment averages ~$318 (SNP) to ~$466 (employer/union), up to ~$577 for the highest parent org

public_reference_figures.source: MedPAC, March 2025 Report to the Congress, Ch. 11 (MA status report)
public_reference_figures.figures: 'quality bonuses will account for about 3 percent (an estimated $15 billion) of MA payments in 2025'; against ~26M bonus-plan enrollees in 2025 that is ~$575/enrollee

reference_figure_notes: the ~$560 and ~$575 per-enrollee figures in estimate_basis are DERIVED ratios (neither source prints an overall per-enrollee average)
$600 is not a ceiling: MedPAC's $15B over its own 69%-of-MA bonus-enrollee count (~24M) implies ~$620/enrollee
KFF's segment averages ($318 SNP / $381 individual / $466 employer) are diluted over ALL enrollees of each plan type, not per-bonus-enrollee — conservative but not apples-to-apples
ACA benchmark growth caps can shrink the realized bonus below 5% (to $0) in capped counties — one more reason $400 is not a floor

framing.unit: counts are the machine fields n_flips_of_record_priced, priced_distinct_contracts, priced_multi_year_contracts and n_rows_counted_never_priced; enrollment totals are enrollee-payment-years; H8547 flips down in CY2025 (1,792) and up in CY2026 (1,553)
framing.time_scope: gross/net totals sum three payment years (CY2025+CY2026+CY2027); they are not an annual rate; print totals as 'summed over payment years 2025 through 2027' with the per-year split
framing.direction_convention: UP = the criterion's answer gains bonus status versus published (denied money); DOWN = loses it (payments above the criterion's answer); both are misallocation, neither prints as a taxpayer cost
framing.temporal_blend: CY2025 is a completed payment year; CY2027 is prospective (estimated on the 2026-07 proxy month); the 6/17/2026 upward-only 2027-QBP recalculation is not decidable at the contract level from the public record (stored check, data/raw/sy2026_recalc2027qbp/)
framing.full_set_split: 18 UP / 62 DOWN QBP-relevant (printed grain; 2 endpoint-conditional UP candidates demoted, listed); 8 PDP counted
framing.conditionality: improvement/CAHPS held at published stars; guardrail against published prior-year boundaries (this-year-corrected, history as published); docsonly score list; 2026 D07 MA-PD, with fewer than five distinct scores (all trimmed scores identical), held at published
